paper.title: Multinomial Logit Contextual Bandits: Provable Optimality and Practicality

unmapped: Feedback is the single item chosen by the user from the offered assortment according to a multinomial logit (MNL) choice model with utilities x_ti^T theta*; not semi-bandit
Assortment of at most K (paper's K, mapped to m) items out of N items (declared N_items); per-item revenues r_ti with |r_ti|<=1 revealed each round; expected revenue is the MNL-weighted revenue
Features x_ti drawn i.i.d. with ||x||<=1 and E[x x^T] >= sigma_0 (Assumption 1)
Assumption 2: p(i|S,theta)p(0|S,theta) >= kappa for all theta within distance 1 of theta*
The learner knows kappa, sigma_0 and the number of items N (used in tuning)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the agent observes feature vectors $x_{ti} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ for every item $i \in [N]$. ... the agent offers an assortment $S_t = \{i_1, \ldots, i_\ell\} \in \mathcal{S}$, $\ell \leq K$, and observes the user purchase decision $c_t \in S_t \cup \{0\}$ ... given by a multinomial logit (MNL) choice model

settings.name_in_paper: MNL contextual bandits with uniform revenue
unmapped: MNL choice feedback: user picks one item (or outside option) from the assortment
Uniform revenue r_ti = r for all items (click-through-rate objective)
Features i.i.d. with ||x||<=1, E[xx^T]>=sigma_0 (Assumption 1); kappa lower bound on p(i)p(0) (Assumption 2); relaxed symmetry p_X(-x)/p_X(x) <= rho_0 (Assumption 3)
The learner knows kappa, sigma_0 and the number of items N (used in q_k and alpha_k)
settings.definition_quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:x_bound}-\ref{assum:rho} hold and the revenue $r_i \equiv r$ is uniform.

conditions: Assumption 1: features i.i.d., ||x_ti||<=1, E[x x^T] >= sigma_0
tuning: alpha_t = (1/(2 kappa)) sqrt(2d log(1+t/d) + 2 log t)
T_0 = O(max{kappa^-2 (d log(T/d) + 4 log T), K/sigma^2})

source.label: thm:expected_regret_ucb-mnl
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:x_bound} and \ref{assum:prob_bound} hold and we run \texttt{UCB-MNL} with confidence width $\alpha_t = \frac{1}{2\kappa}\sqrt{2d \log\left( 1 + \frac{t}{d} \right) + 2\log t }$ and $T_0 = \Ocal(\max\{ \kappa^{-2} \left( d \log(T/d) + 4\log T \right), K/\sigma^2  \})$. Then the expected regret of \texttt{UCB-MNL} is upper-bounded by $\mathcal{R}_T = \mathcal{O}( d\sqrt{ T \log(1 + T/d) \log(T/d)})$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected revenues R_t(S,theta*), so pseudo-regret against per-round optimal assortment. Constant hides 1/kappa. Polynomial time given an assortment optimisation oracle. Independent of N.

bound.expression_latex: \mathcal{R}_T \leq  T_0 + \mathcal{O}(1) + \tilde{\alpha}_T  \sqrt{ dT \log \left( T/d \right)  } = \mathcal{O}\left(  d\sqrt{ T  \log \left(  1 + T/d \right) \log(T/d) }  \right)

tuning: T_0 = ceil(C_0 max{(d + log T)/(sigma_0^2 K), 1/sigma_0})
tilde alpha_t = sqrt(T_0 + (8/kappa) d log(1+t/d) + (8/kappa + 16/3) log(ceil(2 log2(tK/2)) t^4) + 4)

source.label: thm:expected_regret_ucb-mnl-online-update
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $C_0 > 0$, such that if we run \textsc{UCB-MNL} with ``online parameter update'' (Algorithm~\ref{algo:UCB-MNL-online-update}) with confident radius $\tilde{\alpha}_t$ for total of $T$ rounds with $T_0 = ...$ assortment size constraint $K$, then the expected regret of the algorithm with is upper-bounded by $\mathcal{R}_T \leq T_0 + \mathcal{O}(1) + \tilde{\alpha}_T \sqrt{ dT \log(T/d)} = \mathcal{O}( d\sqrt{ T \log(1 + T/d) \log(T/d) })$

results.notes: Formal version of Corollary 1 (O~(d sqrt T)). Assumptions not explicitly listed in the theorem but used in proof (kappa in Lemma 10).

bound.regime: T >= tilde T = Omega(max{log^2(T N log2 T)/d, d^3})

conditions: T >= tilde T = Omega(max{log^2(T N log_2 T)/d, d^3})

source.label: thm:expected_regret_supCb-mnl
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:x_bound} and \ref{assum:prob_bound}, and we run Algorithm~\ref{algo:supCB-MNL} with $T_0 = ...$ and $\alpha = \frac{5}{\kappa} \sqrt{ 2\log(TN \log_2 T)}$ for $T \geq \tilde{T}$ rounds ... Then, the algorithm's expected regret is upper-bounded by $\mathcal{R}_T = \mathcal{O}(  \sqrt{dT \log(T/d) \log (TN \log_2 T)  \log_2 T})$.

results.notes: Main-text Theorem 3 states existence of an algorithm with O~(sqrt(dT)); formal statement in appendix used. Paper calls the algorithm impractical; pruning over assortment sets, so compute not stated.

source.label: thm:expected_regret_DBL-MNL
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:x_bound}-\ref{assum:rho} hold and the revenue $r_i \equiv r$ is uniform. Then the expected regret of \texttt{DBL-MNL} over horizon  $T$  is $\Rcal_T = \Ocal\big( \sqrt{d T \log \left( T/d\right) \log(T N) \log(T) } \big)$.

results.notes: Formal statement adds K <= 18/kappa^4 and uses log_2 T. Episodic doubling; algorithm does not take T as input, so recorded as anytime.
